$comment: Recruitment and onboarding values from the law, for docs/23 and migration 0009. Merge every key and structured field into the employment standards edition in Step 7, before it is tested (AGENTS, How to work). An entry marked verify_at_load blocks activation (RULE_NOT_VERIFIED); a jurisdiction an organization uses with no entry stops with JURISDICTION_RULE_MISSING. CanDo never uses a smaller number than the one here; an organization may choose a stricter one.

keys.candidate_records_retention: Shortest time candidate records (postings, applications, interview notes and scores) must be kept. months: the minimum; from: 'decision' (the hiring decision that affected the candidate) or 'posting_closed' (the day the posting was taken down). A value of 0 months means the law sets no fixed minimum; the organization's own setting then decides (docs/23 §4.4).
keys.sin_due: When the employee must give the SIN, counted from the first day of work. CanDo warns HR before the date passes; an organization's due date may be earlier, never later (docs/23 §6.2).
keys.pay_transparency: Additions to the edition's pay_transparency entries.

nationwide.$comment: Rules that apply to every employer in Canada, whatever the province or federal regulation.

sin_due.cite: CRA, Get the social insurance number from the individual (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/payroll/set-up-new-employee/social-insurance-number.html); Employment Insurance Regulations

candidate_records_retention.cite: Personal Information Protection Act (BC), s. 35(1): personal information used to make a decision that directly affects the individual is kept at least one year after it is used
Employment Standards Act, 2000 (Ontario), record-keeping for publicly advertised job postings and application forms, in force 2026-01-01 (same rule as pay_transparency.posting_records_years)
Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Quebec): information used to make a decision about a person is kept at least one year after the decision
Personal Information Protection Act (Alberta) s. 35: kept only as long as reasonably required for legal or business purposes; no fixed minimum found

pay_transparency.cite: Pay Transparency Act (NL), 2022: the pay history ban is in force; the posting range requirement is not yet in force

candidate_records_retention.cite: PIPEDA applies to private employers' candidate data only in part; no fixed minimum found

pay_transparency.cite: Secondary sources describe a ban on pay history questions in interviews; not confirmed

candidate_records_retention.cite: PIPEDA principle 4.5: keep information used to make a decision long enough for the person to have access; no fixed number
